objectives.text: Reflect on lessons learned from the 2023 large bank failures and discuss how best to ensure the safety and soundness of the banking system going forward, including preliminary thoughts on targeted regulatory enhancements.

citations.quote:
Today, I would like to talk about bank liquidity risk. With the one-year anniversary of 
last year’s large bank failures fast approaching, it is a good time to reflect on lessons learned and 
to discuss how best to ensure the safety and soundness of the banking system going forward.

objectives.text: Diagnosis: the failures of SVB and Signature Bank highlighted three previously underappreciated vulnerabilities — the speed of uninsured deposit withdrawal, insufficiency of liquid-asset holdings absent operational capacity to monetize them, and contagion via 'guilt by association' rather than direct interconnectedness.

citations.quote:
The failures of Silicon Valley Bank (SVB) and Signature Bank last year highlighted three 
vulnerabilities that had been underappreciated:

Third, contagion to healthy banks does not require interconnectedness and direct 
exposure to a failing bank. Systemic threats can occur via “guilt by association,” i.e., 
shared uncertainty with regards to seemingly similar risk profiles, such as high 
reliance on uninsured deposits for funding.

objectives.text: Diagnosis: bank utilization of the discount window faces two structural hurdles — an operational hurdle (lack of pre-positioned, ready-to-pledge collateral) and a stigma hurdle (fear that borrowing signals weakness and exacerbates a run).

citations.quote:
Bank utilization of the Federal Reserve’s 
discount window faces two hurdles, however. The first is operational.

The second hurdle to discount window borrowing is stigma. Since the 2008 financial 
crisis, banks have worried that news of their borrowing from the discount window could be 
perceived as a sign of weakness, thereby exacerbating a run.

As such, many banks believe that in 
stress they will face a Hobson’s choice: the option of borrowing from the discount window is not 
a real one in practice.

objectives.text: Diagnosis: some high-risk deposits, including uninsured deposits, are miscategorized as 'retail demand deposits' under the LCR, producing an under-calibration of risk.

citations.quote:
One problem 
highlighted by the failures of SVB, Signature, and Credit Suisse, is that some high-risk deposits, 
including uninsured deposits, are categorized as “retail demand deposits” for LCR purposes, 
resulting in an under-calibration of risk.

objectives.text: Proposal: a new targeted regulatory requirement for midsize and large banks to hold sufficient liquidity to cover stress outflows over a five-day period, with the numerator counting the liquidity value of pre-positioned discount-window collateral (in addition to reserves) and limited to covering only acute, ultra-short-term outflows.

citations.quote:
I believe it is more appropriate and prudent to take a 
narrower approach and limit discount window credit to covering only acute, ultra-short-term 
outflows—up to, say, five days—through a new, targeted liquidity requirement.

In short, I believe a new targeted regulatory requirement for midsize and large banks to 
have sufficient liquidity to cover stress outflows over a five-day period warrants serious 
consideration. The denominator should consider the potential speed and severity of uninsured 
deposit outflows, while the numerator should consider the liquidity value of pre-positioned 
discount window collateral, in addition to reserves.

objectives.text: Proposal: the rule should clarify operational preparedness expectations related to the discount window, potentially including a requirement to conduct periodic test draws.

citations.quote:
The rule should also clarify operational 
preparedness expectations related to the discount window, perhaps even including a requirement 
to do periodic test draws.

objectives.text: Proposal: explicitly giving banks credit for discount-window borrowing capacity (to cover ultra-short-term, acute outflows) to make clear regulators expect stressed banks to use the window, thereby helping to de-stigmatize its use, while rejecting the broader approach of adding discount-window capacity to the LCR numerator itself.

citations.quote:
One solution would be to explicitly give banks credit for their discount window 
borrowing capacity to cover ultra-short term, acute outflows like those endured by SVB and 
Signature.

Some have argued for adopting this approach within the LCR by adding discount window 
capacity to the numerator and expanding the sources of liquidity beyond high quality liquid 
assets (HQLA). That would be dangerous.

objectives.text: Proposal/hope: credibly classifying and differentiating deposit types (e.g., operational vs. non-operational) to help contain the scope of 'guilt by association' and mitigate contagion risk, pursued via an OCC economics symposium on deposit gathering, franchises, and risk profiles.

citations.quote:
Our hope is that focusing on this may contribute to efforts to credibly classify and differentiate 
deposit types, which may help contain the scope of any “guilt by association” and thus help 
mitigate contagion risk in the future.

in June the OCC will host an economics symposium for 
invited academic and government researchers on deposit gathering, franchises, and risk profiles.

objectives.text: Forward-looking objective: banks and regulators should start working now on building appropriate risk management and controls ('better brakes') for a faster, always-on, real-time payments and tokenization environment.

citations.quote:
Banks and regulators should start working now on building the right brakes 
for a more real-time financial system.

definitions.definition: Requires large banks to hold high quality liquid assets sufficient to meet stressed liquidity outflows over a 30-day period.

citations.quote:
requires large banks to hold high quality liquid assets sufficient to meet stressed liquidity

expanding the sources of liquidity beyond high quality liquid

definitions.definition: An LCR deposit category assigned a low (10%) stress outflow rate reflecting assumed 'stickiness'; the speech notes some high-risk/uninsured deposits are categorized here, producing under-calibration of risk.

citations.quote:
By contrast, the outflow 
rate for retail demand deposits is low—10%—reflecting their stickiness.

definitions.definition: The phenomenon, dating from the 2008 financial crisis, whereby banks worry that news of their borrowing from the discount window could be perceived as a sign of weakness, thereby exacerbating a run, such that many banks believe borrowing in stress is not a real option (a 'Hobson's choice').

citations.quote:
Since the 2008 financial 
crisis, banks have worried that news of their borrowing from the discount window could be 
perceived as a sign of weakness, thereby exacerbating a run.

definitions.definition: Shared uncertainty with regard to seemingly similar risk profiles (e.g., high reliance on uninsured deposits for funding), which can produce systemic contagion threats to healthy banks absent interconnectedness or direct exposure.

citations.quote:
Systemic threats can occur via “guilt by association,” i.e., 
shared uncertainty with regards to seemingly similar risk profiles, such as high 
reliance on uninsured deposits for funding.

definitions.definition: A distinction between the portion of uninsured deposits used to fulfill specific business purposes (e.g., meeting payroll or paying suppliers) ('operational') and the portion representing excess funds, which has a riskier liquidity profile ('non-operational'); banks define these differently and there is no standardized classification system.

citations.quote:
This is the distinction between so-called “non-operational” and 
“operational” deposits. Banks define these differently, however, in part because their customers 
and business models vary enormously, and there is no standardized classification system that 
market participants can see and trust.

definitions.definition: (undefined here) — used throughout without a formal definition beyond descriptive statistics (e.g., growth from $2.3 trillion in 2009 to $7.7 trillion in 2022) and behavioral characterization (rapid, mass withdrawal capability).

citations.quote:
Uninsured deposits in aggregate 
have grown considerably since 2009.

definitions.definition: The Federal Reserve's real-time, inter-bank, 24/7/365 gross settlement payment system, with which financial institutions can settle payment transactions any time, including nights, weekends, and holidays.

citations.quote:
The Federal Reserve’s FedNow service is a real-time, inter-bank, 24/7/365 gross 
settlement payment system.

definitions.definition: (undefined here) — described as banks identifying ex ante the assets that will be pledged to the discount window as collateral and arranging them accordingly, to mitigate operational timing risk.

citations.quote:
This timing 
risk can be mitigated by banks identifying ex ante the assets that will be pledged to the discount 
window as collateral and pre-positioning them accordingly.

citations.quote:
Some have argued for adopting this approach within the LCR by adding discount window 
capacity to the numerator and expanding the sources of liquidity beyond high quality liquid 
assets (HQLA). That would be dangerous.

references: Remarks by Vice Chair for Supervision Michael S. Barr, The Importance of Effective Liquidity Risk Management (December 1, 2023)

citations.quote:
Remarks by Vice Chair for Supervision Michael S. Barr, The Importance of Effective Liquidity Risk Management 
(December 1, 2023). It is worth recalling Walter Bagehot’s dictum, from his 1873 book, Lombard Street: A 
Description of the Money Market: to avert panic, central banks should lend early and freely, to solvent firms, against 
good collateral, and at "high” rates.

notes: Per ceiling note, this source is a reform proposal/horizon item: all proposed regulatory content (the five-day targeted liquidity requirement, pre-positioned discount-window collateral credit, periodic test draws, LCR deposit reclassification, deposit-type standardization) is extracted only as objectives (stated) and interactions, never as operative obligations, since the speech does not itself impose binding duties. The source contains an internal tension preserved as-written: Hsu explicitly rejects one variant of discount-window-credit-in-LCR ('That would be dangerous') while endorsing a narrower, separate five-day requirement achieving a related aim — this is extracted as stated, not resolved. The source does not address FHLB collateral/operational rules, Call Reports, or FR 2052a, and does not mention McKernan; those scope elements are absent from this particular item and are not fabricated here.
